title: Add Grafana dashboards + alerts for audit log delivery lag and drop rate
author: Aisha Bello
release_notes:
- New Grafana dashboard: Audit Logs / Delivery (lag + drop rate + exporter health)
- New Grafana dashboard: Audit Logs / SLO Overview (burn rates + error budget)
- Alert rules + suggested paging thresholds for delivery lag and drops (non-paging warnings included)
- Runbook links added to alert annotations
description:
Summary: Adds two Grafana dashboards and a first-pass alerting policy for the audit log pipeline. This is intended to support the audit logging schema + coverage initiative by making delivery lag and drops measurable, actionable, and consistent across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

Motivation: We’ve had a few recent backlogs where audit events were delayed (exporter queue growth / consumer saturation). For enterprise readiness we need (1) a clear SLO view and (2) paging thresholds that are conservative enough to catch real data loss, but not so aggressive that on-call gets paged for small transient spikes.

What’s included: 1) Dashboard: “Audit Logs / Delivery” with panels for end-to-end lag, stage-by-stage lag, enqueue/persist/export rates, drop counters, DLQ growth, exporter per-sink errors, and a breakdown by environment/region. 2) Dashboard: “Audit Logs / SLO Overview” with SLO target, error budget burn, and quick links for investigations. 3) Prometheus alert rules: - AuditLogDeliveryLagP99High (paging): p99 delivery lag > 300s for 10m (per env+region). - AuditLogDeliveryLagP95High (warning): p95 delivery lag > 120s for 15m. - AuditLogDropRateHigh (paging): drop rate > 0.05% for 10m (computed as dropped / enqueued, with guards for low traffic). - AuditLogExporterSinkErrorsHigh (warning): exporter sink delivery errors sustained (per sink type). - AuditLogDLQGrowthHigh (warning): DLQ size increasing for 20m.

Suggested SLO/threshold rationale (documented in dashboard + alert annotations): - We are targeting “99% of events exported within 60s” for steady state. P95 >120s is treated as early warning; P99 >300s sustained is paging (customer-visible risk and potential data loss if backlog + retention windows collide). - Drop rate paging is set at 0.05% sustained; this should be close to zero in normal conditions. We still keep a separate warning for any non-zero drops but avoid paging on single increments.

Metrics assumptions: This PR relies on the audit log pipeline metrics introduced in redwood PR 18488 / exporter PR 232 (enqueue/persist/export counters + lag histograms). We intentionally do not introduce new metrics here; this is a packaging/standardization layer.

Implementation notes: - Uses templated variables: env, region, sink, service. - Lag queries use histogram_quantile() on auditlog_delivery_lag_seconds_bucket with explicit rate windows. - Drop rate uses clamp_min(enqueued, 1) to avoid division by zero and excludes canary namespaces by default.

Rollout plan: Ship to staging first, validate alert noise for 48h, then enable paging rules in prod behind the existing SRE alert routing (audit-log pipeline on-call). Warnings can go live immediately.

Links: - Linear: ENG-2489 (delivery lag SLO/dashboards), ENG-2488 (exporter reliability) - Runbook (draft): confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/audit-log-delivery-lag-runbook (linked from alert annotations) - Related incident thread: #incidents (audit-log exporter backlog) - This PR does not change customer-facing behavior; it’s operational readiness work.
commits: grafana: add audit logs delivery dashboard (lag, rate, drop, exporter health)
grafana: add SLO overview dashboard with burn rates and links
alerts: add audit log delivery lag p95/p99 rules with annotations
alerts: add drop rate + DLQ growth + exporter sink error rules
docs: add runbook links and panel descriptions; tidy variable naming
ci_summary: Checks: lint (pass), unit (pass), dashboard-json-validate (pass), promtool-check (pass), package (pass).
review_conversation: Miles Thornton: Can we justify paging at p99>300s? On bad days we’ve seen p99 around 2–3m with no true drops, but still painful. Also please ensure the query window doesn’t hide spikes.

Aisha Bello (author): Added rationale in the alert annotation + dashboard description. Kept p99>300s but require 10m sustained; p95 warning catches earlier. Also changed rate window from 10m to 5m for lag histograms to be more responsive while still stable.
Rafael Mendes: Drop rate query needs a guard for low volume, otherwise it’ll page on 1 drop / 1 enqueue in a quiet env. Also consider excluding load-test namespaces.

Aisha Bello (author): Updated drop rate to use clamp_min(enqueued, 100) for paging evaluation and added a separate warning rule that triggers for any non-zero drops only when enqueued>5k/10m. Excluded namespaces matching `loadtest|perf` in the default dashboard filter.
Allison Grant: Naming: can we standardize alert names with the telemetry standards? Also please add runbook_url annotation; our routing expects it for paging alerts.
Aisha Bello (author): Renamed rules to AuditLogDeliveryLagP99High / AuditLogDropRateHigh etc. Added runbook_url + dashboard_url annotations for all paging alerts.
Nadia Rahman: Dashboard looks good. One nit: stage-by-stage lag panels should call out that ‘persisted’ is pipeline storage, not exporter sink ack. Can we add panel help text?
Aisha Bello (author): Added panel descriptions and clarified the semantics in the “How to read this dashboard” text block.

Sean Gallagher: Approved once the DLQ growth alert is warning-only; paging should remain for drops/lag only. Also make sure these alerts are scoped per env+region so one bad region doesn’t mask another.
Aisha Bello (author): DLQ growth is warning-only. All rules group by env+region and include labels for routing.
post_merge_notes: Follow-ups: (1) Enable paging rules in prod after 48h staging soak and confirm no noisy alerts; (2) Update the runbook with screenshots of new dashboards; (3) Verify alert routing for the audit-log pipeline on-call matches the new rule labels.
